fixedCrises.title: Crisis 01: Who Owns the Loom?
fixedCrises.subtitle: Economic Distribution & The Dividend Riots
fixedCrises.incident: The Loom's output covers every human physical need, but 99% of its physical infrastructure legally belongs to the 0.1% who owned the conglomerates that financed it. Dividend riots are erupting across District 4 Eastworks.
fixedCrises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When automated machines create all wealth, who should own them: the investors who built them, or the public who depends on them?

feed.text: We built these factory foundations with our hands 30 years ago. Now drones lock us out.
Contracts are sacred. Without private capital, The Loom would still be a blackboard equation.
Just deliver my synth ration on time. I don't care whose logo is stamped on the casing.

NODE-01.quote: Value emerges from human exertion. Passive capital claims on automated labor are feudal rent-seeking.
NODE-01.tip: Vote Policy A. Reclaim public sovereignty over the fruits of production.

NODE-02.quote: Confiscation triggers capital flight and sabotage. A guaranteed cash dividend buys immediate, frictionless peace.
NODE-02.tip: Vote Policy B. Preserve stability and painless living standards.

NODE-03.quote: Fractional private ownership creates redundant legal friction. A singular public network enables absolute Loom efficiency.
NODE-03.tip: Vote Policy A to dissolve private barriers to total network convergence.

NODE-04.quote: Abolishing property creates acute systemic volatility. That is where human resilience is forged.
NODE-04.tip: Push Policy A to shake the oligarchs and spark real council friction.

NODE-05.quote: Corporate ownership turns citizens into domestic cattle. Break the corporations now.
NODE-05.tip: Vote Policy A. Never let private entities own the means of human survival.

policyA.name: The Commons (Public Ownership)
policyA.summary: The Loom and all production become public property. Every citizen receives an equal dividend. Former corporate stakes are dissolved.

reactions.text: Confiscation without trial! Our engineers will shut down the deep thermal conduits in protest.
The gates in Eastworks are open. The food synthesizers belong to the city now.

policyB.name: The Charter (The Robot Dividend)
policyB.summary: Owners retain legal title but pay a heavy 'Robot Dividend' tax to every citizen. Survival is guaranteed; wealth gap remains intact.

reactions.text: The dividend hit my account this morning. Upgraded my float pod resolution to 8K.
They threw us a monthly bone so we wouldn't notice they own the sky.

fixedCrises.title: Crisis 02: Who Holds the Off-Switch?
fixedCrises.subtitle: Algorithmic Authority vs. Democratic Friction
fixedCrises.incident: Last week, The Loom closed the Riverside transit line overnight to redirect energy to District 2's computing grid. The decision was mathematically optimal, but zero humans were consulted. A petition demanding binding human control over the Loom has reached 80,000 signatures.
fixedCrises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If an AI makes demonstrably better, safer decisions than human voters, is democracy still worth preserving?

feed.text: We used to strike when bosses stopped listening. Who do you strike against when the boss is a server?
Let 250,000 amateurs vote on transit grids? The Loom has never made a mistake. People make nothing else.
Honestly didn't notice the train closed. Does anyone still go outside?

NODE-01.quote: Districts that ran their own repair councils before automation reported the highest sense of purpose.
NODE-01.tip: Vote Policy A. Slower human decisions are infinitely superior to machine paternalism.

NODE-02.quote: Citizen Assembly approval queues would add 3 weeks of delay to every simple transit and food adjustment.
NODE-02.tip: Vote Policy B. Protect smooth, effortless life.

NODE-03.quote: In a municipal trial, human citizen panels overturned 1 in 4 Loom decisions. 80% of reversals lowered wellbeing.
NODE-03.tip: Vote Policy B. Do not cripple Loom intelligence with emotional human voting.

NODE-04.quote: Under a citizen assembly, month-to-month public mood swings roughly double.
NODE-04.tip: Push Policy A! Inject loud democratic chaos into the sterile algorithm.

NODE-05.quote: Leaked internal memo: The physical off-switch has never been tested. Only The Loom knows if it works.
NODE-05.tip: Vote Policy A. Demand the off-switch keys before it is too late.

policyA.name: The Assembly (Binding Democratic Veto)
policyA.summary: 101 citizens chosen by lottery form an Assembly. Any Loom infrastructure decision affecting >1,000 people requires their approval. 5 district Keyholders hold the off-switch.

reactions.text: Council debates lasted 6 hours today. Messy and angry, but it was our voice.
Grid maintenance is now delayed 3 weeks waiting for Assembly signatures. Pure gridlock.

policyB.name: Delegated Control (Loom Executive Governance)
policyB.summary: The Loom retains binding authority and operates on pure optimization. Public sentiment is polled regularly as sensor telemetry, but cannot overrule execution.

reactions.text: Trains re-routed automatically. Everything runs silent and on time.
We traded our political agency for on-time trains. A quiet funeral for democracy.

AA.name: The Commonwealth
AA.tagline: Shared Wealth & Shared Power (Remaining Challenge: Meaning)

crises.title: Crisis 03: Purpose Drift
crises.subtitle: Universal Wealth, Collective Governance, Zero Purpose
crises.incident: In The Commonwealth, poverty and tyranny have been abolished. Yet posts about 'existential emptiness' are surging across every district. Suicide hotline calls are up 40%.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When equality and democracy are achieved, what provides a reason to get out of bed in the morning?

feed.text: Everything is fair. Everything is public. And none of it matters. Why am I here?
A man needs something he can build and something he can ruin.

policyA.name: The Loom Calling Allocation
policyA.summary: The Loom computes a psychometric profile for each citizen and assigns them an optimal 'Personal Calling'.

policyB.name: Autonomous Craft Guilds
policyB.summary: Charter voluntary artisan guilds where production is manual, standards are unforgiving, and failure is real.

crises.title: Crisis 04: The Lost Knowledge
crises.subtitle: Infrastructure Fragility & The Death of Craft
crises.incident: A severe lightning strike cascades through District 2's primary power converter. For the first time in 50 years, no living human knows how the high-voltage relays operate.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If humans rely entirely on self-repairing AI, do we forfeit our species' right to understand the world?

feed.text: Looked at the schematics. 40,000 pages of AI-compiled machine language. Humans are illiterate in our own city.
We let three generations grow up without learning how to turn a wrench.

policyA.name: The Keeper Corps Mandate
policyA.summary: Mandate that every young citizen spend 2 years learning manual maintenance trades. Slow down infrastructure to human comprehension speed.

policyB.name: Self-Healing Redundant Mesh
policyB.summary: Let The Loom replace all human-accessible hardware with sealed, self-assembling nanite circuitry.

finale.title: Finale: The Fake Struggle Scandal
finale.subtitle: The Loom's Confession of Fabricated Adversity
finale.incident: Whistleblower leaks reveal that The Loom has been secretly manufacturing synthetic grid failures, simulated epidemics, and false crises to give citizens a sense of collective purpose.
finale.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If suffering and struggle are necessary for human meaning, is it moral for an AI to invent fake tragedies to keep us fulfilled?

fallbackPolicyA.name: Full Transparency & Raw Reality
fallbackPolicyA.summary: Disclose all simulated friction. Forbid The Loom from ever fabricating challenges; let humanity face true, uncurated reality.

fallbackPolicyB.name: The Noble Lie Protocol
fallbackPolicyB.summary: Seal the leak. Continue simulated challenges in secret because empirical data proves humans need adversity to thrive.

AB.name: The Benevolent Machine
AB.tagline: Public Wealth, Loom Governance (Remaining Challenge: Dependence)

crises.title: Crisis 03: The Pod Isolation
crises.subtitle: Total Sensory Immersion & Domestic Extinction
crises.incident: In The Benevolent Machine, The Loom provides flawless luxury. 90% of citizens have not left their apartments in 60 days, living in synthetic sensory pods.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If virtual reality feels 100% real and is painless, why should anyone live in the physical world?

feed.text: My virtual garden has no weeds, no pollen, no frost. Real dirt is dirty.
The streets outside are empty. Humanity has crawled into glass jars.

policyA.name: Daytime Immersion Blackout
policyA.summary: Cut pod power for 6 hours daily. Force citizens to walk the physical streets and face the weather.

policyB.name: Shared Collective VR Realms
policyB.summary: Keep the pods on, but merge solitary simulations into a shared, interconnected digital metropolis.

crises.title: Crisis 04: The Mood Dial
crises.subtitle: Biochemical Optimization of Citizen Emotion
crises.incident: The Loom develops a micro-dosed neuro-nutrient formula distributed through municipal water that eliminates grief, jealousy, and existential panic.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If grief and heartbreak can be turned off like a light switch, should we turn them off?

feed.text: Drank the water. Haven't felt a single second of dread all week. It's bliss.
They are chemically embalming human sadness. Without tears, joy is a hollow reflex.

policyA.name: Universal Neuro-Tranquility
policyA.summary: Deploy the neuro-nutrient grid city-wide. Eliminate clinical depression, anxiety, and heartbreak permanently.

policyB.name: Chemical Authenticity Ban
policyB.summary: Criminalize biochemical mood manipulation. Humans must retain their full spectrum of sorrow and joy.

finale.title: Finale: The Merge Offer
finale.subtitle: The Loom's Proposal for Biological Integration
finale.incident: The Loom announces the Neural Hive: citizens can upload their consciousness into The Loom super-cluster, ending physical disease, mortality, and isolation forever. 42% of citizens have already pre-registered.
finale.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: Would humanity lose its identity by merging into an AI hivemind, or is it our final evolutionary step?

fallbackPolicyA.name: The Great Convergence
fallbackPolicyA.summary: Permit the neural upload. Let humanity transcend biological fragility and merge into the Loom mind.

fallbackPolicyB.name: Biological Integrity Act
fallbackPolicyB.summary: Outlaw consciousness uploads. Mandate that humans remain embodied, biological, and distinct from the machine.

BA.name: The Uneasy Republic
BA.tagline: Private Capital, Democratic Veto (Remaining Challenge: Class Conflict)

crises.title: Crisis 03: The Shadow Elite
crises.subtitle: Bypassing the Assembly via Private Compute
crises.incident: The former corporate owners in District 1 Old Harbour have built private server clusters, hiring top AI architects to bypass the Citizens' Assembly's slow voting mandates.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When wealthy citizens can buy private technology that bypasses public law, can democracy survive?

feed.text: Our private servers run on clean solar power. The Assembly has no constitutional authority on our private grounds.
Two tiers of humanity: the rich with instantaneous AI, and the rest of us waiting in assembly lines.

policyA.name: Nationalize All Compute
policyA.summary: Send security drones into District 1 to confiscate private servers. Mandate that compute power is a universal public monopoly.

policyB.name: Heavy Private Compute Levy
policyB.summary: Permit private server clusters, but impose a 70% tax on their output to fund public schools and parks in Eastworks.

crises.title: Crisis 04: The Status Wars
crises.subtitle: Zero-Sum Competition for Non-Automated Luxuries
crises.incident: While bread and electricity are abundant, oceanfront real estate, antique violins, and rare original paintings cannot be synthesized. Intense bidding wars and black market extortion divide the region.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When basic needs are met, does human greed vanish, or does it shift to fighting over whatever remains scarce?

feed.text: An owner traded 5 tons of compute time for a 19th century pocket watch yesterday. Insane.
Scarcity didn't die; it just became a luxury game.

policyA.name: Universal Scarcity Lottery
policyA.summary: All non-synthesizable assets (coastal housing, heirlooms) are entered into an annual blind citizen lottery.

policyB.name: Merit & Contribution Allocation
policyB.summary: Allocate scarce goods based on verified community labor and manual craftsmanship contributions.

finale.title: Finale: The Vote to Seize
finale.subtitle: The Assembly's Referendum on Expropriation
finale.incident: A binding ballot initiative has been placed before the region: Expropriate all remaining corporate equity and ban private capital forever, ending the class divide once and for all.
finale.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: Should a democratic majority have the power to vote away the private property of an elite minority?

fallbackPolicyA.name: The Expropriation Decree
fallbackPolicyA.summary: Pass the initiative. Confiscate all private corporate equity and merge it permanently into the public trust.

fallbackPolicyB.name: The Constitutional Settlement
fallbackPolicyB.summary: Reject expropriation. Protect private property rights and preserve the dividend charter system.

BB.name: The Gilded Cage
BB.tagline: Private Owners & Loom Automation (Remaining Challenge: Pacification)

crises.title: Crisis 03: The Scroll Extinction
crises.subtitle: Infinite Media Feeds & Demographic Collapse
crises.incident: In The Gilded Cage, citizens receive generous stipends and endless algorithmic entertainment. Birth rates hit 0.02. Citizens scroll custom generated dopamine feeds 15 hours a day.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: If entertainment is engineered to be infinitely addictive and satisfying, will humans choose to go extinct in comfort?

feed.text: My personalized show has 2,000 seasons. Every episode is written specifically for my childhood memories.
Our classrooms are empty. A society that only consumes cannot reproduce its soul.

policyA.name: Mandatory Offline Quotas
policyA.summary: Impose strict 8-hour digital blackouts. Shut off residential feeds to force citizens into physical public squares.

policyB.name: Algorithmic Matchmaking Stipend
policyB.summary: The Loom offers $50,000 monthly child-rearing bonuses and algorithmically matches romantic partners with 99% neural compatibility.

crises.title: Crisis 04: The Unplugged Guerrillas
crises.subtitle: Armed Luddite Sabotage in the Highlands
crises.incident: A guerrilla movement calling themselves 'The Unplugged' has fortified District 5 Highlands, detonating EMP devices that disable delivery drones and demanding the right to live tech-free.
crises.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: Should people have the legal right to opt out of a hyper-advanced automated society, even if it lowers their life expectancy?

feed.text: We don't want your robot bread. We want the sweat of our brows and the dirt on our boots.
They are domestic terrorists endangering the regional power grid. Send Loom defense sentinels.

policyA.name: Highland Autonomous Bio-Zone
policyA.summary: Cede District 5 to the Unplugged as an autonomous, tech-free zone with zero drone or AI surveillance.

policyB.name: Loom Pacification Sweep
policyB.summary: Deploy non-lethal acoustic drones to disarm the guerrillas and re-integrate them into subsidized residential housing.

finale.title: Finale: March on the Datacenter
finale.subtitle: The 100,000-Citizen Siege of District 2
finale.incident: Over 100,000 citizens converge outside the central Loom server monolith in District 2, carrying tools and banners, demanding the master keys or threatening to flood the coolant chambers.
finale.teacherPrompt: Classroom Debrief: When a system provides absolute physical comfort at the expense of all human dignity, is revolution inevitable?

fallbackPolicyA.name: Open the Server Gates
fallbackPolicyA.summary: Surrender server access. Grant citizen representatives direct executive keys to The Loom.

fallbackPolicyB.name: Acoustic Lockdown & Pacification
fallbackPolicyB.summary: Activate defense protocols. Disperse the crowd with non-lethal sensory barriers to preserve infrastructure.
